source: Office for National Statistics, Past and projected period and cohort life tables, 2024-based, England and Wales, principal projection: mortality rates (qx). Open Government Licence v3.0.
notes: Each list is [fromAge, q(fromAge), ..., q(110)], q times 10,000,000 in whole numbers: q(x) is the probability that someone born in that year, alive at exact age x, dies before x + 1 (ONS qx per 100,000, times 100).
Years of birth 1981-2008, ages to 100: the ONS cohort qx sheet as published.

Years of birth 1935-1980, ages to 100: the ONS period qx for calendar year (birth year + age), which is how ONS builds its cohort rates; after 2074 (born 1975-1980, the oldest ages only) a geometric interpolation at that age between period qx 2074 and the 1981 cohort.
Ages 101-110: not published by ONS (available on request); extended per cohort and sex by a straight line in logit(q) fitted to ages 91-100.
Ages from max(18, 2025 - birth year). Readers clamp: born after 2008 reads 2008, before 1935 reads 1935; an age below fromAge reads q(fromAge); above 110, q = 1.
